To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in maturatig SHRs, the levels of cytokines, and chemokines were significantly reduced, while oxidative stress was significantly elevated in the pancreas.
the pancreatic cytokine levels are reduced in mature SHRs, while the levels of the oxidative stress markers, malondialdehide and thiobarbituric acid reactive substances are elevated.
in juvenile SHRs the pancreatic levels of RANTES were significantly reduced, while the pancreatic concentrations of malondialdehydes were significantly decreased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel hypothesis that the pancreas of maturating SHR may be a site of inflammation suppression and oxidative damage, which could contribute to the development of hypertension.
the role of cytokines, inflammatory mediators, and oxidative stress during the development of hypertension.
the pancreatic cytokines and oxidative damage in juvenile and mature SHRs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alterations/abnormality of cytokine and chemokine contents in the pancreas and oxidative damage in maturating SHR are the consequence of the development and progression of hypertension.
the pancreatic inflammation and oxidative damage are involved in the development of hypertension in maturating animals.
the pancreatic levels of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines and chemotactic factors do not differ between juvenile SHRs and WKYS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytokines and oxidative stress markers are altered in the pancreas at the early stage of hypertension development.
the pancreatic cytokine and chemokine alterations are not involved in the pathogenesis of hypertension in SHR rats, but the increased oxidative damage is.
in SHRs, there are significant alterations in the cytokine/chemokine profile and oxidative stress in the pancreas, which may be related to pancreatic damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in SHRs, the pancreas is involved in hypertension development.
the cytokine/chemokine alterations in the pancreas may be associated with the development of hypertension.
the pancreas is not only an important organ in the pathogenesis of hypertension, but also an important target for hypertension-related damage.
